main.description: One member's response to a network.essmesh.governance.proposal record. See ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.9 -- an ordinary signed record from the member's own individual key, never a threshold or aggregated operation. A Proposal becomes a de facto Ratification purely by count: N distinct, valid 'consent' Signals referencing it, no separate record or signature required to mark that. 'exit' is the one type with a defined mechanical effect beyond information -- see ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.8's fission discussion.

subject.description: AT-URI + CID of the network.essmesh.governance.proposal record this responds to. Pinning the CID, not just the URI, means a Signal is unambiguous about exactly which version of a Proposal it consented to, even if the author edited it after some members already signaled -- an edit produces a new record version a stale Signal doesn't cover.

signalType.description: This is not yes/no by design -- see ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.9 on why collapsing it would be a regression. 'consent' is the only type that counts toward a Ratification threshold. 'block' has no cryptographic effect of its own (ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.9's 'What a block Signal actually does, and doesn't do') -- it's a social fact an honest client is expected to honor by refusing to act on the Proposal, not something this schema can enforce. 'exit' shrinks the effective governance-eligible roster per ESS_MESH_SPEC.md 3.8, independent of whichever Proposal it's attached to -- an exit is about the signaler's own standing, not a response to that specific proposal's content.

text.description: Free text -- 'I'll go along but want my concern noted,' or a block's stated reason. This is where the actual deliberation lives; the protocol doesn't parse or act on it.
